items.title: Anthropic closes debut at $97.17, then slides in second day
items.take: Opened its first day at $111.50, briefly topping a $2 trillion market cap, and closed Thursday at $97.17, 17% above its $83 IPO price. Friday it gave back about 9% as investors booked profits on the largest IPO in history.

items.title: Worst week in over a year even after the IPO
items.take: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq are on course for their worst weekly performances in over a year despite the blockbuster debut; the Nasdaq slid more than 1% at Friday's open while the Dow rose. Meta is off 4% and Microsoft 3% as AI financing doubts spread.

items.title: Chip stocks tumble around the world before the US open
items.take: Nvidia fell about 4% premarket Friday, a 35% one-month slide despite record revenue, and semiconductor names dropped across Asia and Europe. Amazon and Alphabet, Anthropic's largest shareholders, feel its post-IPO slide directly.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin seek to project power at their first summit
items.take: The first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen produced a four-point peace declaration and a dialogue on nuclear nonproliferation, but no Ukraine breakthrough. The joint statement did include cooperation on AI safety to prevent security threats.

items.title: U.S. Floats NATO Membership for Ukraine
items.take: Today's morning podcast covers Washington floating NATO membership for Ukraine in a peace plan, plus the market fallout from Anthropic's debut. A good 10-minute catch-up before class.
